requirements.title: Existing registration, sign-in, sessions and profiles
acceptance: Preserve secure sessions, profile settings and account-scoped authorization.

requirements.title: Existing communities, one administrator and multiple moderators
acceptance: Preserve community discovery, role separation and exactly one active administrator.

requirements.title: Blockchain-inspired responsive interface and networking
acceptance: Keep branding, community connections, mobile navigation and accessible layouts.

requirements.title: Existing proposals, simulated treasury and immutable audit history
acceptance: Preserve legacy proposals, balanced ledger history, replay and overspending protection.

requirements.title: Simple dashboard and deep analytics extras
acceptance: Keep dashboard customization, saved views, filters, source inspection, exact currency groups and CSV exports.

requirements.title: Existing multi-scheme rounds and two equal-weight sealed elections
requirements.baselineEvidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md: 20 round scenarios and 14 accessibility scans
acceptance: Preserve member/public submissions, frozen voters, 24-hour screening and separate FPTP selection, stage privacy and published results.

requirements.title: Contribution declarations for every member including the creator
acceptance: New strict-profile membership records include a declared contribution, questions and introduction as applicable, including the founding administrator.
Legacy unknown pledges remain unknown; declarations never masquerade as received funds.

requirements.title: PDF-conforming governance with governed administrator succession
acceptance: New strict-profile admissions require member majority with published quorum; removal requires exact two-thirds of valid YES/NO power.
An administrator can be removed through a member decision with an eligible, published successor and atomic authority transfer.
Preserve legacy REVIEW and transfer behavior as versioned extras; staff receive no voting privilege from role alone.
Strict-profile staff cannot use unilateral suspension or voter stripping to shape an open ballot; legacy emergency suspension remains an explicitly versioned extra with regression coverage.

requirements.title: Staff-only, member and everyone submission policies
acceptance: Add STAFF, retain MEMBERS and EVERYONE, and enforce each policy server-side.
Staff publish agendas; permitted members and outsiders submit schemes, with clear funding-request categories and recipient information.

requirements.title: Immutable versioned governance and asset snapshots
acceptance: Preserve published V1 rounds as equal-weight, decision-only rounds without retroactive payment rights.
New funded rounds lock all supported rules, asset ID/decimals, deadlines, caps and settlement policy before contributions/votes.
Unsupported future veto/method settings are rejected rather than silently ignored.

requirements.title: Prepaid round funds with contributor ownership and segregation
acceptance: Record actual simulated received contributions separately from pledges and communal legacy funds.
Move committed amounts into scoped held/reserved accounts so legacy TREASURY spending cannot consume them.
Every deposit is balanced, replay-safe, attributable and reconciled per round and asset.

requirements.title: Published contribution limits, targets and collection cutoff
acceptance: Publish minimum/maximum contributions, target, cutoff and failed-target/empty-round behavior.
Freeze the paid contribution basis at the declared cutoff; later deposits never alter an open electorate or its weights.

requirements.title: Winner-all settlement and exact contributor refunds
acceptance: Deliver a full local funded FPTP round with explicitly veto-disabled rules, safe winner-all settlement and receipts.
Ties, no quorum, no eligible schemes, failed targets, unused caps and refunds have published deterministic handling.
Refund the original contributor/payment source even after membership changes; preserve exact minor units and replay safety.

requirements.title: Separate financial lifecycle and durable execution recovery
acceptance: Keep election state separate from collection/reservation/execution/refund state and immutable posted history.
Use unique operation identities and durable outbox/attempt records; external submission is never inside a retryable database transaction.
Concurrent settle/refund/retry and restart cases cannot double-spend or double-refund.

requirements.title: Equal and paid-contribution-weighted votes by stage
acceptance: Configure screening, selection and veto weights independently, using immutable eligible paid-contribution snapshots.
Publish quorum/approval/abstention denominators; reject all-zero weighted electorates and never sum different assets.
Deposits, departures and role changes after cutoff do not rewrite frozen power or valid earlier ballots.

requirements.title: Winner-all, proportional and custom ranked allocation
acceptance: Support all three policies with published request caps, tie handling, too-few-winner and residual rules.
Ranked shares validate to 100%; integer deterministic remainder allocation preserves every minor unit.
A versioned immutable allocation plan is the sole source of payout instructions.

requirements.title: Optional 24-hour, 90-percent rejection veto
acceptance: Publish enabled/disabled and equal/weighted veto configuration before funding and freeze its electorate/power.
When enabled, show the result/allocation then hold all payouts through the full 24-hour window.
At least 90% of all frozen eligible veto power rejects the whole round; successful rejection refunds contributors.

requirements.title: Central settlement gates and exact conservation across allocation modes
acceptance: Every controller, worker, legacy bridge and retry uses the same eligibility gate; configured vetoes cannot be bypassed.
Received = held + reserved + paid + refunded per round/asset, with fees zero unless explicitly versioned and published.
Unknown execution outcomes reconcile before new submission or release; no hidden redistribution of unused shares.

requirements.title: Optional capped contribution-weighted mode
acceptance: Only implement as a separately named published option with satisfiable caps and exact frozen weights; ordinary contribution weighting remains available.

requirements.title: Ranked-choice/IRV selection
acceptance: Validate ranked ballots and publish elimination, exhaustion and tie rules.
Provide deterministic replay and reference/edge-case tests with equal and defined weighted ballots.

requirements.title: Multi-winner STV selection
acceptance: Version the quota, seat count, surplus-transfer precision and tie rules; test quota and conservation vectors.
Keep elected winners distinct from the separate money-allocation policy.

requirements.title: Elo-style pairwise polling
acceptance: Publish initialization, K/update order or period semantics, draws, pair scheduling and tie rules before voting.
Validate pairwise ballots and deterministic result transcripts; distinguish Elo from Glicko-2.

requirements.title: Glicko-2 replaces the document's GECCO label
acceptance: Use GLICKO_2 with rating, deviation, volatility, rating-period and convergence parameters.
Pass Mark Glickman's official example vectors for the standard algorithm; separately specify/test any weighted extension.
Never relabel Elo or a generic pairwise score as Glicko-2.

requirements.title: Forced-choice pairwise plus-one/minus-one polling
acceptance: Support one-versus-one comparisons without a draw, with published +1/-1 scoring and declared weight treatment.
Reject duplicate, incomplete/ineligible and out-of-round pairs according to the published ballot contract.

requirements.title: All-method privacy, result/weight/allocation compatibility and replay
acceptance: All six methods retain frozen eligibility, one immutable complete ballot per permitted unit and stage-specific secrecy across UI, analytics, audits and exports.
Publish each method's ranking, ties, support measure and allocation transformation; do not proportionally divide raw Elo/Glicko ratings into money.
Define and test the supported equal/weighted and allocation combinations before exposing them; never silently substitute a method or omit a required feature.

Close all 36 required cells in workflow/method-matrix.json (six methods, two weight modes, three allocation policies) with named semantics and evidence; an unresolved mandatory cell blocks Part 4 unless the user explicitly approves an exclusion.

requirements.title: One-to-five-star member, scheme/proposal and agenda/round reviews
acceptance: Support every required target with a 1-5-star score and written review, aggregate counts and average.
Separate presentation/participation reviews from verified recipient performance; no invented project-outcome claims.

requirements.title: Participation-qualified reputation and accountable moderation
acceptance: Require recorded shared participation, reject self/duplicate/ineligible reviews and keep edit/moderation history.
Provide abuse reports, moderation reasons and appeals without silently rewriting historical outcomes or raw ratings.

requirements.title: Secure wallet ownership, explicit testnet assets and contract integration
acceptance: Link wallets with expiring domain/network-bound single-use signed challenges and replay protection.
Deploy/test a treasury contract with scoped authorization, operation nonces and immutable allocation references.
Keep native NEAR precision and asset identity distinct from USD/BDT/EUR; protect keys and disclose the governance/custody trust model.
Contract-level tests reject wrong signer/round/asset/recipient, over-allocation, duplicate nonce, redirected refunds and payout-before-veto bypasses.

requirements.title: Real NEAR testnet deposit, payout and refund finality proof
acceptance: Obtain genuine wallet approvals/funding and execute a testnet deposit, payout and refund through the app/contract.
Independently query RPC at FINAL and verify successful receipt outcomes plus signer, receiver, actions, amount, asset, network and operation identity.
A compiled adapter, mock receipt, transaction hash alone or unperformed external action cannot satisfy completion.

requirements.title: Live outbox reconciliation, failure handling and restart recovery
acceptance: Lost responses, RPC failures, worker restart, duplicate callbacks and pending operations reconcile without duplicate external transfers.
A final failure safely releases/resolves reservations; an unknown status does not trigger an unsafe refund or retry.
Dispatch live execution separately from the global legacy simulation adapter; account for gas/storage through a separate operating reserve and reconcile custody against principal liabilities.

requirements.title: Integrated deep analytics for every new subsystem
acceptance: Extend the existing simple overview/drill-down model to round funds, weighted elections, allocations, vetoes, refunds, ratings and chain observations.
Preserve saved views/customization and add scoped source links/CSV; hidden ballots never leak through reports, search, aggregates or exports.
Reconcile each monetary/currency/asset group without assumed FX or fabricated historic counts.

requirements.title: Reusable templates and explicit lifecycle maintenance
acceptance: Allow reusable agenda templates while each published round keeps its immutable rule version.
Provide idempotent scheduled/manual finalization and recovery tools with logs; unauthorized staff cannot override locked outcomes.

requirements.title: Operational handoff and sensitive-action hardening
acceptance: Provide environment validation, public health/diagnostic boundaries, backup/restore instructions and a verified recovery exercise in isolated data.
Require appropriate reauthentication for sensitive authority/wallet actions and preserve account/session abuse controls.
Document remaining production limitations honestly; do not enable mainnet or publish a hosted deployment implicitly.

requirements.title: Reproducible large fictional demo and separate real-chain demonstration
acceptance: Provide an opt-in isolated 100-member, 100,000-BDT, three-scheme demonstration showing sealed voting, allocation and refund paths.
Demonstrate real testnet assets separately without pretending BDT values are NEAR or resetting the user's demo database.

requirements.title: Final full-requirements audit and verified release handoff
acceptance: Every mandatory requirement has implementation and fresh check/review evidence, including actual NEAR finality artifacts.
Run migration, money/privacy/authorization, HTTP, browser, accessibility, production-build and independent-review gates against the final source snapshot.
Do not convert deferred, unverified or externally blocked mandatory work into complete status.

requirements.title: Preserve all existing extra features and user data throughout
acceptance: Every part retains existing navigation, dashboards, deep analytics, saved views, CSV, community networking, legacy proposals, treasury receipts and immutable history.
Use additive/versioned migrations; no fabricated pledges, ownership, hashes, confirmations, or destructive demo resets.
Legacy public ballots remain clearly identified as historical behavior, while new PDF-conforming flows use the documented secrecy rules.
